# Cohomology Operations and Eilenberg–MacLane Spaces

## Statement

Let $\pi$ be an abelian group and $n > 1$. A **cohomology operation of type $(n, \pi, m, \pi')$** is a natural transformation
$$\theta : H^{n}(-;\pi) \longrightarrow H^{m}(-;\pi').$$
Such operations are in natural one-to-one correspondence with elements of $H^{m}(K(\pi,n);\,\pi')$, where $K(\pi,n)$ is the Eilenberg–MacLane space of type $(\pi,n)$.

## Proof

### Setup

Fix an Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(\pi,n)$ with a chosen fundamental class
$$\iota_n \in H^{n}(K(\pi,n);\pi).$$
Recall that $K(\pi,n)$ represents the functor $H^{n}(-;\pi)$ on the homotopy category of CW-complexes: for every CW-complex $X$ and every $\alpha \in H^{n}(X;\pi)$, there is a homotopy class of maps $f_\alpha : X \to K(\pi,n)$, unique up to homotopy, such that
$$\alpha = f_\alpha^{*}(\iota_n).$$
This is the universal property of $K(\pi,n)$: the bijection
$$[X, K(\pi,n)] \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} H^{n}(X;\pi), \qquad [f] \mapsto f^{*}(\iota_n)$$
is natural in $X$.

### The correspondence

We define two maps between the set of operations and the cohomology group.

**From operations to cohomology classes.** Given a natural transformation $\theta : H^{n}(-;\pi) \to H^{m}(-;\pi')$, apply it to the universal class:
$$\Phi(\theta) := \theta_{K(\pi,n)}(\iota_n) \;\in\; H^{m}(K(\pi,n);\pi').$$

**From cohomology classes to operations.** Given $u \in H^{m}(K(\pi,n);\pi')$, define for every CW-complex $X$:
$$\Psi(u)_X : H^{n}(X;\pi) \to H^{m}(X;\pi'), \qquad \Psi(u)_X(\alpha) := f_\alpha^{*}(u),$$
where $f_\alpha : X \to K(\pi,n)$ is the classifying map of $\alpha$, i.e. $f_\alpha^{*}(\iota_n) = \alpha$.

### $\Psi(u)$ is well-defined

If $f_\alpha$ and $f'_\alpha$ both classify $\alpha$, they are homotopic, so $f_\alpha^{*}(u) = (f'_\alpha)^{*}(u)$. Hence $\Psi(u)_X(\alpha)$ depends only on $\alpha$, not on the representative.

### $\Psi(u)$ is a natural transformation

Let $g : Y \to X$ be a map of CW-complexes. We must show commutativity of
$$\require{AMScd}\begin{CD} H^{n}(X;\pi) @>{\Psi(u)_X}>> H^{m}(X;\pi')\\ @V{g^{*}}VV @V{g^{*}}VV \\ H^{n}(Y;\pi) @>{\Psi(u)_Y}>> H^{m}(Y;\pi')\end{CD}$$

For $\alpha \in H^{n}(X;\pi)$ with classifying map $f_\alpha : X \to K(\pi,n)$, the class $g^{*}\alpha \in H^{n}(Y;\pi)$ is classified by $f_\alpha \circ g : Y \to K(\pi,n)$, since
$$(f_\alpha \circ g)^{*}(\iota_n) = g^{*}f_\alpha^{*}(\iota_n) = g^{*}\alpha.$$
Therefore
$$\Psi(u)_Y(g^{*}\alpha) = (f_\alpha \circ g)^{*}(u) = g^{*}f_\alpha^{*}(u) = g^{*}\Psi(u)_X(\alpha).$$
This proves naturality.

### The two constructions are inverse

**$\Phi \circ \Psi = \mathrm{id}$.** For $u \in H^{m}(K(\pi,n);\pi')$, the classifying map of $\iota_n \in H^{n}(K(\pi,n);\pi)$ is the identity $\mathrm{id} : K(\pi,n) \to K(\pi,n)$. Hence
$$\Phi(\Psi(u)) = \Psi(u)_{K(\pi,n)}(\iota_n) = \mathrm{id}^{*}(u) = u.$$

**$\Psi \circ \Phi = \mathrm{id}$.** Let $\theta$ be an operation and set $u = \Phi(\theta) = \theta_{K(\pi,n)}(\iota_n)$. For any $X$ and $\alpha \in H^{n}(X;\pi)$ with classifying map $f_\alpha$:
$$\Psi(u)_X(\alpha) = f_\alpha^{*}(u) = f_\alpha^{*}\bigl(\theta_{K(\pi,n)}(\iota_n)\bigr).$$
By naturality of $\theta$ applied to $f_\alpha : X \to K(\pi,n)$:
$$f_\alpha^{*}\bigl(\theta_{K(\pi,n)}(\iota_n)\bigr) = \theta_X\bigl(f_\alpha^{*}(\iota_n)\bigr) = \theta_X(\alpha).$$
Hence $\Psi(\Phi(\theta)) = \theta$.

### Conclusion

The maps $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are mutually inverse bijections, natural in the evident sense. Therefore:

> **Cohomology operations of type $(n,\pi,m,\pi')$ are in natural bijection with $H^{m}(K(\pi,n);\,\pi')$.**

Under this bijection, the operation $\theta$ corresponds to its value $\theta(\iota_n)$ on the fundamental class of $K(\pi,n)$, and conversely a class $u \in H^{m}(K(\pi,n);\pi')$ defines the operation $\alpha \mapsto f_\alpha^{*}(u)$ via pullback along the classifying map.

**Consequence (Yoneda-style remark).** This is an instance of the Yoneda lemma: the functor $H^{n}(-;\pi)$ is represented by $K(\pi,n)$, so natural transformations out of it are classified by their value on the universal element $\iota_n$, i.e. by elements of the representing object's cohomology $H^{m}(K(\pi,n);\pi')$.

### PROOF COMPLETE
